name: Boundary pivot
summary: An internal Pauli spider connected to a boundary spider can be removed by pivoting, leaving a Hadamard on the boundary wire.
description:
A variant of the [pivot simplification](../pivot/) for an internal Pauli spider $u$ (phase $j\pi$) that is connected to a spider $v$ on a boundary wire, with any phase $\alpha$. Pivoting along $uv$ removes $u$. The phase $\alpha$ of $v$ becomes a phase gadget connected to the former neighbours of $u$ (as in the [gadget pivot](../pivot-gadget/)), and the boundary wire is now attached, through a Hadamard, to a new spider with phase $j\pi$ that is connected to the former neighbours of $u$. Shared neighbours of $u$ and $v$ get $(j+1)\pi$, neighbours of only $v$ get $j\pi$.

Together with the gadget pivot this allows removing every internal Pauli spider in a graph-like diagram. The Duncan–Kissinger–Perdrix–van de Wetering simplification achieves the same by first unfusing the boundary spider (see [graph-like identity removal](../graph-like-identity-removal/)) and then applying the ordinary pivot. As in the gadget pivot, the hub of the gadget carries $j\pi$, which is equivalent to a phase-free hub with leaf $(-1)^j\alpha$.
parameter_notes: n_u, n_w and n_v are the numbers of neighbours of only u, of both, and of only v (shown for n_u = 2, n_w = 0, n_v = 1; shared neighbours of u and v also get connected to the gadget and to the new boundary spider, and get (j+1)π added). The neighbours may have any number of further legs and edges.
conditions: u is internal and has a Pauli phase jπ; v has exactly one boundary wire.
